stem: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom is called an __________.
solution: An element is a pure substance made up of only one kind of atom.

stem: Which of the following is an element?
solution: Oxygen is an element; water and salt solution are compounds/mixtures and air is a mixture.

stem: Elements are broadly classified as metals, non-metals and __________.
solution: Elements are grouped as metals, non-metals and metalloids.

stem: A substance formed by the chemical combination of two or more elements in a fixed ratio is a __________.
solution: A compound is formed when elements combine chemically in a fixed proportion.

stem: Water is a compound made of the elements __________.
solution: Water (H₂O) is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

stem: Common salt is a compound of the elements __________.
solution: Common salt (sodium chloride, NaCl) is made of sodium and chlorine.

stem: The properties of a compound are __________ those of its constituent elements.
solution: A compound has new properties, different from those of the elements that formed it.

stem: A material made of two or more substances mixed physically, not chemically, is a __________.
solution: A mixture is a physical combination of substances that keep their own properties.

stem: In a mixture, the components __________.
solution: The components of a mixture keep their individual properties and can be separated.

stem: A mixture in which the composition is uniform throughout is called a __________ mixture.
solution: A homogeneous mixture has the same composition throughout, like sugar dissolved in water.

stem: A mixture in which the components are not uniformly distributed is called a __________ mixture.
solution: A heterogeneous mixture has an uneven composition, like sand mixed with iron filings.

stem: Air is an example of a __________.
solution: Air is a homogeneous mixture of gases such as nitrogen and oxygen.

stem: A mixture of iron filings and sulphur can be separated using a __________.
solution: Iron is magnetic, so a magnet separates the iron filings from the sulphur.

stem: A mixture of sand and water can be separated by __________.
solution: Filtration separates insoluble sand from water.

stem: Salt can be recovered from salt solution by __________.
solution: Evaporating the water leaves the dissolved salt behind.

stem: A solution consists of a __________ dissolved in a solvent.
solution: A solution is made of a solute dissolved in a solvent.

stem: In sugar solution, the solvent is __________.
solution: In sugar solution, water is the solvent and sugar is the solute.

stem: The smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction is an __________.
solution: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that participates in reactions.

stem: Two or more atoms joined together form a __________.
solution: A molecule is formed when two or more atoms combine.

stem: The symbol 'O' stands for the element __________.
solution: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen.

stem: The chemical symbol for the element gold is __________.
solution: The symbol for gold is Au (from its Latin name aurum).

stem: The chemical formula of carbon dioxide is __________.
solution: Carbon dioxide has the formula CO₂ — one carbon and two oxygen atoms.

stem: Which of the following is a compound?
solution: Carbon dioxide is a compound; the others are elements.

stem: Which of the following is a mixture?
solution: Sea water is a mixture of water and dissolved salts; the others are pure substances.

stem: The components of a compound can be separated only by __________ methods.
solution: Elements in a compound are chemically bonded and can be separated only by chemical means.

stem: The components of a mixture can usually be separated by __________ methods.
solution: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods like filtration, evaporation and using a magnet.

stem: Sublimation can be used to separate a mixture of common salt and __________.
solution: Ammonium chloride sublimes on heating, separating it from salt that does not.

stem: The process used to separate two miscible liquids with different boiling points is __________.
solution: Distillation separates miscible liquids by exploiting their different boiling points.

stem: The process of separating lighter husk from heavier grain using wind is called __________.
solution: Winnowing uses wind to blow away the lighter husk, separating it from grain.

stem: Separating cream from milk using a spinning machine uses the process of __________.
solution: Centrifugation spins the mixture so that denser and lighter components separate.

stem: The colours in black ink can be separated by __________.
solution: Chromatography separates dissolved substances (like ink dyes) based on how they move on paper.

stem: Which of the following is a pure substance?
solution: Distilled water is a pure compound; the others are mixtures.

stem: An alloy such as brass is best described as a __________.
solution: An alloy is a mixture of metals (brass is copper and zinc).

stem: A metalloid shows properties of __________.
solution: Metalloids, like silicon, have some properties of metals and some of non-metals.

stem: In a compound, the elements are always combined in a __________ ratio by mass.
solution: A compound has a fixed ratio of its constituent elements by mass.

stem: In a mixture, the substances can be present in __________ proportions.
solution: Mixtures can have their components in any proportion.

stem: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
solution: Sugar solution is uniform throughout — a homogeneous mixture.

stem: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
options: A mixture of oil and water
solution: Oil and water do not mix uniformly, forming a heterogeneous mixture.

stem: Rusting of iron forms a new substance (rust), showing it is a __________.
solution: Rust (iron oxide) is a new compound formed by a chemical change.

stem: The number of naturally occurring elements is a little over __________.
solution: There are a little over 90 naturally occurring elements.

stem: Which of the following is the correct chemical symbol for sodium?
solution: Na is the symbol for sodium (from Latin natrium).

stem: Milk is best described as a __________.
solution: Milk is a mixture (a colloid) of fat, water, proteins and other substances.

stem: The separation of a solid dissolved in a liquid by first heating to vapour and then cooling the vapour is called __________.
solution: Distillation vaporises the liquid and condenses it back, leaving the dissolved solid behind.

stem: Which of these can be separated using filtration?
solution: Insoluble chalk powder can be filtered out of water.

stem: A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by any chemical method is an __________.
solution: Elements are the simplest substances and cannot be broken down chemically.

stem: The energy change in the formation of a compound from its elements shows that __________.
options: a chemical reaction has taken place
solution: Energy is often absorbed or released when a compound forms, indicating a chemical reaction.

stem: Brass, bronze and steel are examples of __________.
solution: These are alloys — mixtures of metals with improved properties.

stem: The main difference between a compound and a mixture is that a compound has a __________.
solution: A compound has a fixed composition and new properties, unlike a mixture.

stem: Which of the following methods would best separate coloured pigments in a leaf extract?
solution: Chromatography separates the different coloured pigments dissolved in the extract.

stem: The most fundamental idea of this chapter is that matter can be classified as __________.
solution: Matter is classified into elements, compounds and mixtures based on its composition.

stem: A substance that is made up of only one kind of atom is called an:
solution: An element is a pure substance made up of only one kind of atom; it cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means (e.g. hydrogen, oxygen, iron, gold).

stem: The smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction is an:
solution: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that retains its properties and can take part in a chemical reaction.

stem: A substance formed by the chemical combination of two or more elements in a fixed ratio is a:
solution: A compound is a pure substance formed by the chemical combination of two or more elements in a fixed proportion (ratio); e.g. water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

stem: Water (H2O) is an example of a(n):
solution: Water is a compound made of the elements hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined in a fixed ratio (2:1); its properties are different from those of hydrogen and oxygen.

stem: A material made by simply mixing two or more substances in any proportion, without a chemical reaction, is a:
solution: A mixture is formed by physically mixing two or more substances (elements or compounds) in any proportion, without a chemical reaction; the components retain their properties (e.g. air, saltwater).

stem: In a compound, the properties of the substance are ______ those of its constituent elements.
solution: In a compound, the properties are entirely different from those of its constituent elements; e.g. water (a liquid that puts out fire) is very different from hydrogen (flammable) and oxygen (supports burning).

stem: In a mixture, the components:
options: Retain their individual properties and can be separated by physical methods
solution: In a mixture, the components keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods (like filtration, evaporation), since no chemical reaction has occurred.

stem: A mixture in which the components are uniformly mixed (same throughout) is called a:
solution: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout (the components are evenly mixed and not distinguishable), e.g. salt dissolved in water (a solution).

stem: A mixture in which the components are not uniformly mixed and can be seen separately is called a:
solution: A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, with the different components visible or distinguishable, e.g. a mixture of sand and iron filings.

stem: A homogeneous mixture of a solute dissolved in a solvent is called a:
solution: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of a solute (the substance dissolved) in a solvent (the dissolving medium), e.g. sugar or salt dissolved in water.

stem: In a salt solution, salt is the ______ and water is the ______.
solution: In a salt solution, salt is the solute (the dissolved substance) and water is the solvent (the substance that dissolves it).

stem: Elements are represented by short forms called:
solution: Each element is represented by a symbol — usually the first one or two letters of its name (e.g. H for hydrogen, O for oxygen, Fe for iron, Na for sodium).

stem: The symbol for the element iron is:
solution: The symbol for iron is Fe, derived from its Latin name 'Ferrum'. Many elements have symbols based on their Latin names.

stem: The symbol for the element sodium is:
solution: The symbol for sodium is Na, derived from its Latin name 'Natrium'.

stem: Elements are broadly classified into metals, non-metals and:
solution: Elements are classified into metals, non-metals, and metalloids (which show properties of both metals and non-metals, e.g. silicon).

stem: A compound of carbon and oxygen that we breathe out is:
solution: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a compound of carbon and oxygen; it is produced during respiration and breathed out, and used by plants in photosynthesis.

stem: A chemical formula, like H2O, tells us:
options: The elements present and the number of atoms of each in a compound
solution: A chemical formula shows the elements present in a compound and the number of atoms of each (e.g. H2O means two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom).

stem: The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods such as:
options: Filtration, evaporation, distillation and magnetic separation
Only heating to very high temperatures
solution: The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods like filtration, evaporation, distillation, sieving, magnetic separation and hand-picking, since no chemical bonds need to be broken.

stem: A magnet can be used to separate iron filings from a mixture because iron is:
solution: Iron filings can be separated from a mixture (e.g. with sand) using a magnet, because iron is magnetic and gets attracted to the magnet while the other component does not.

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a compound from a mixture? (i) A compound forms by chemical combination in a fixed ratio (ii) A mixture forms by physical mixing in any ratio (iii) A compound has new properties
solution: All three are correct: a compound forms by chemical combination in a fixed ratio and has new properties, whereas a mixture forms by physical mixing in any ratio and retains the components' properties.

stem: Common salt (sodium chloride) is a compound of the elements:
solution: Common salt (sodium chloride, NaCl) is a compound of the metal sodium and the non-metal chlorine, chemically combined in a fixed ratio.

stem: There are about how many naturally occurring elements known?
solution: There are about 90 naturally occurring elements; in total over 110 elements are known (including some made artificially), all arranged in the Periodic Table.

stem: The overall importance of classifying matter into elements, compounds and mixtures is that it helps us:
options: Understand the composition of substances and how to separate or combine them
solution: Classifying matter into elements, compounds and mixtures helps us understand the composition and properties of substances, and how they can be separated, combined or used in daily life and industry.
